observation.visible_scene: A young man wearing glasses, a black hooded sweatshirt with a white chest logo, a teal band on his right wrist and a dark watch on his left wrist stands indoors beneath a curved brushed-metal ceiling, in front of a row of vertical pillars and glass panels (an escalator is faintly visible behind the glass). He holds a kendama toy: a glossy purple-pink ball (tama) attached by a yellow-green string to a handle (ken). Throughout the excerpt he keeps the toy in front of his torso and continuously repositions both hands and forearms, drawing, looping and crossing the string so that the ball travels along it relative to his hands.
visible_changes: The purple ball shifts position along the string frame to frame: it starts high near the raised right hand (frame 1), drops to the left hand (frame 2), is hidden between the joined hands (frames 3-4), reappears mid-string as the hands separate (frames 5-9), then moves to the left-hand side as the right hand extends forward (frame 10).

The forearms cross in front of the body around frames 11-12 and again more horizontally around frames 23-28, during which the ball is partly or fully occluded by the arms/hands (e.g. frames 3, 4, 11, 26) and emerges at different heights (low at frame 12, high near the face at frames 27-28).

From about frame 13 to 21 the right hand is held flat or pinches the string near the upper body while the ball hangs lower on the string, then the string opens into a triangular/V shape with the ball at the bottom vertex (frames 22-24) and again at the lower-left (frames 32-35).

In the later frames (29-41) the right hand grips the handle while the left hand opens palm-up, the string is drawn taut and swung horizontally (frame 31), and the ball ends at the lower-left with the string crossed between the hands (frame 41).

The background (metal ceiling, pillars, glass, escalator) stays fixed in position across all frames, indicating the camera is stationary and the apparent motion is from the person's hands and the toy, not from camera movement.
The person's body and head remain roughly in place, leaning slightly and watching the toy; only his arms, hands and the kendama move appreciably.
outside_clip_unknowns: The name or intended result of the kendama trick is not determinable from the frames.
What happened before t=0 (how the toy was launched or handed) and what happens after t=2.667 (whether the ball is caught on a cup, released, or dropped) are outside the segment.
Whether the ball ever makes contact with the handle's cups or spike is not clearly shown; the clip only shows it suspended on the string and passing near the hands.
uncertain_details: In frames where the arms/hands overlap the ball (3, 4, 11, 26), the ball's exact position is obscured by occlusion rather than absent.
The precise points where the string loops over fingers versus the handle are hard to resolve at this frame rate.
Small hand motions between consecutive frames may reflect either deliberate string manipulation or incidental adjustment; the excerpt does not let this be separated cleanly.
